grammar.title: Subject–Verb Agreement with Long Subjects
grammar.explanation: Ignore prepositional phrases (of, along with, in addition to) between the head noun and the verb. Match the verb strictly to the main head noun.
grammar.example: The results of the latest semiconductor efficiency test are promising.

vocabulary.sentence: The current bandwidth is adequate for daily emails, though not for large data transfers.
Management decided to allocate 20% of the annual budget to R&D.
Raw material costs rose sharply; consequently, profit margins narrowed in Q3.

speaking_prompt: How would you explain a sudden project delay to an international client diplomatically without sounding defensive?

quiz.question: The primary objective of these newly introduced training modules ____ to enhance cross-cultural communication.

grammar.title: Formal Conditional Inversion (Should / Were / Had)
grammar.explanation: In formal corporate communication, omit 'if' and invert the auxiliary verb (Should, Were, Had) with the subject.
grammar.example: Should you require further assistance, please contact the HR department.

vocabulary.sentence: All suppliers must comply with international environmental regulations.
Senior engineers were initially reluctant to adopt the new software interface.
The contract will be renewed provided that all performance metrics are met.

speaking_prompt: Describe a situation where you had to persuade a reluctant colleague or student to try a new method.

quiz.question: ____ the company to expand overseas, it would need bilingual corporate trainers.
quiz.rationale: 'Were + subject + to-infinitive' is the formal inversion for Second Conditional.

grammar.title: Conjunctions vs. Prepositions of Contrast
grammar.explanation: Use 'Although / Even though' before a full clause (Subject + Verb). Use 'Despite / In spite of' before a noun phrase or gerund (-ing).
grammar.example: Despite having sufficient funding, the project was delayed due to supply chain bottlenecks.

vocabulary.sentence: We do not have sufficient evidence to justify a full product recall.
Offering clear career progression is crucial to retain top-performing staff.
The market forecast was pessimistic. Nevertheless, our division exceeded its target.

speaking_prompt: What strategies can tech companies use to retain top talent in a competitive industry?

quiz.question: ____ the high cost of implementation, the board approved the new system.
quiz.rationale: 'The high cost of implementation' is a noun phrase, so it requires the preposition 'Despite'.
